battle.name: 黑鷹戰爭
battle.theater: 巴茲艾克斯河與密西根河匯流處
battle.brief: 一八三二年四月，黑鷹率五百戰士與六百老幼再渡密西根河入伊利諾伊州；八月二日，其部眾在威斯康辛河下游的巴茲艾克斯河畔遭美軍正面擊潰，主力星散，旋西遷，戰事以美方全勝告終。輪發手槍這類十六世紀的西班牙鎖匠舊物，一八三二年早已讓位於燧發手槍，只在軍械庫中留作祖型。

kit.name: 輪發手槍
kit.history: 最早的後膛手槍。機械太貴，只給火槍隊的軍官與近衛。

countries: 美方是聯邦正規軍與伊利諾伊州民兵合組的聯軍。聯邦方面，西部軍區的正規步兵由准將亨利·阿特金森指揮，他於四月十二日進駐羅克島的阿姆斯特朗堡，四月組織「邊疆軍」：正規步兵六百二十九人、騎馬民兵志願者三千一百九十六人，後者編成三個旅，由亞歷山大·波西、彌爾頓·亞歷山大、詹姆斯·D·亨利三位旅將率領，扣除地方巡邏與警衛任務後，實際可作戰者約四百五十名正規兵與二千一百名民兵；伊利諾伊州長約翰·雷諾茲以民兵少將身分隨軍，惠特塞德、斯提爾曼等各團團長各領一營，亨利·道奇則自帶二百五十人的騎兵營。聯邦軍當時沒有常設騎兵，追擊全靠臨時招募的志願騎手。與美方並肩作戰的還有霍奇克、梅諾米尼、達科他與波塔瓦托米等族武裝，約七百餘人，多擔任嚮導、搜索與追殘部的任務。索克方則是黑鷹的「英國支隊」：索克、麥斯基維基與基卡普人，核心是五百名戰士，連同老幼共約一千一百人；指揮層是黑鷹這位戰時首領，加上尼亞波與瓦博基謝克，首領權分散，沒有歐式參謀體系。索克與福克斯兩族的主權首領基奧庫克與瓦佩洛選擇不參戰，反而站到美方一邊。
countriesEn: The American side was a joint force of federal regulars and Illinois state militia. On the federal side the regular infantry of the Western Department was under Brigadier General Henry Atkinson, who took post at Fort Armstrong on Rock Island on 12 April; in April he organized the Army of the Frontier, consisting of 629 regular infantry and 3,196 mounted militia volunteers, the latter divided into three brigades commanded by the brigadier generals Alexander Posey, Milton Alexander and James D. Henry. Once local patrol and guard duties were subtracted, roughly 450 regulars and 2,100 militiamen were actually available for campaigning. The governor of Illinois, John Reynolds, accompanied the force as a major general of militia; regimental commanders such as Whiteside and Stillman each led a regiment, and Henry Dodge brought a mounted battalion of 250 men of his own. The federal army had no standing cavalry at the time, so all pursuit depended on hastily recruited volunteer horsemen. Fighting alongside the Americans were Ho-Chunk, Menominee, Dakota and Potawatomi detachments, more than 700 men in all, employed mostly as guides, search parties and hunters of the remnants. The Sauk side was Black Hawk's British Band: Sauks, Meskwakis and Kickapoos, with a core of 500 warriors and about 1,100 people counting the women and children. The command consisted of Black Hawk as war chief, together with Neapope and Wabokieshiek; authority was divided and there was no European-style staff system. The civil chiefs of the Sauk and Fox nations, Keokuk and Wapello, chose not to fight and instead stood on the American side.
people: 黑鷹是索克族出生在索肯努克的戰時首領，年輕時隨部落西遷，後來堅持返回密西根河與羅克河交會處的老村；他並非世襲的和平首領，只是在一八三二年成為隊伍的實際帶隊人。他的謀士尼亞波既是戰時首領，也是代表族人同美方簽約、傳話的人；瓦博基謝克則是族中的宗教領袖兼世俗首領，人稱「溫尼巴戈先知」，其先知鎮聚落住著約二百名不滿現任首領的異議者。索克部落在聖路易條約的問題上分成兩派，主和的基奧庫克勸族人遷往密西根河西岸，卻仍被要求代表全族出面談判。美方人物同樣密集：阿特金森是全戰役的聯軍統帥，但被批評為紙上將軍，遲疑而缺乏決斷；州長雷諾茲反而主戰，急著把索克人趕出伊利諾伊；惠特塞德率民兵旅沿羅克河搜索，屢屢失去敵蹤；少校斯提爾曼在五月十二日擅自離營追敵，營地於五月十四日入夜遭黑鷹四十名戰士襲擊，十二名民兵陣亡；少校哈克爾頓同日擅自獵殺一名索克人，成為導火線。六月十五日，傑克遜不滿阿特金森的處置，越過他任命斯科特接掌戰局；斯科特從東部各站湊得約九百五十人，卻在霍亂中損失慘重，最後一艘汽船抵達芝加哥時只剩約三百五十名可用之兵，趕到前線已錯過戰鬥。曾在此役嶄露頭角的還有駐紮威斯康辛的正規步兵柴契利·泰勒、傑斐遜·戴維斯與羅伯特·安德森：泰勒在八月受命看管投降的黑鷹，戴維斯與安德森則押解俘虜順密西根而下。伊利諾伊民兵中的林肯時年二十三歲，當選自己那一連的連長，因身高六呎四吋被同袍戲稱「長腿上尉」，全役未曾接戰。混血商人皮埃爾·帕凱特在七月中旬提供的情報，把美軍引向黑鷹的營地，是戰局的轉折之一。
peopleEn: Black Hawk was the Sauk war chief born at Saukenuk, who had gone west with his people in his youth and later insisted on returning to the old village at the junction of the Rock River and the Mississippi; he was not an hereditary peace chief, only the man who actually led the column in 1832. His advisers included Neapope, who was both a war chief and the man who signed agreements and carried messages for his people with the Americans, and Wabokieshiek, the religious and civil leader known to the Americans as the Winnebago Prophet, whose settlement of Prophetstown held about two hundred malcontents. The Sauks were split over the Saint Louis treaty: Keokuk, who led the accommodationist faction and urged his people to move west of the Mississippi, was nevertheless required to speak for the nation in negotiation. The American side was just as crowded. Atkinson was the overall commander of the combined force, but he was criticized as a paper general who hesitated and would not commit. Governor Reynolds, by contrast, wanted the war. Whiteside led the militia brigade up the Rock River but repeatedly lost the enemy trail. Major Isaiah Stillman left camp in pursuit on 12 May; his bivouac was attacked by Black Hawk's warriors after dark on 14 May, and twelve militiamen were killed. Major Samuel Hackelton on 12 May killed a Sauk on his own initiative after pursuing a small party flying a red flag, and that killing lit the fuse. On 15 June President Jackson, dissatisfied with Atkinson's handling of the war, appointed Winfield Scott to take command. Scott collected about 950 men from eastern posts, but cholera had already broken out among them; by the time his last steamboat reached Chicago he had only some 350 effective soldiers, and he reached the front too late to take part in any fighting. Others who distinguished themselves here included Zachary Taylor, Jefferson Davis and Robert Anderson, all of the 1st Infantry: Taylor took charge of the surrendered Black Hawk in August, and Davis and Anderson escorted the prisoners down the Mississippi. Abraham Lincoln, then twenty-three, served in the Illinois militia, was elected captain of his company, and was nicknamed Captain Long by his comrades for his six-foot-four frame; he saw no combat throughout. The intelligence supplied by the métis trader Pierre Paquette in mid-July, which pointed the Americans at Black Hawk's camp, was one of the turning points of the war.
kits: 這張卡上的兵器是輪發手槍，十五世紀末西班牙與北義大利鎖匠的製品：槍尾是一支盛底火藥的尾栓，中段有主發條筒與棘輪，發條推動齒輪輪軸，擊錘上的燧石擦過輪面取火。整支槍的造價遠高於同期火槍，上膛又慢、必須雙手操作，因此從來只配給火槍隊的軍官與近衛，而不是列陣的士卒。到了一八三二年，這種機構早已被燧發擊錘取代兩百年，實際上不會出現在戰場上：美軍正規步槍是一八一六年式點五四口徑燧發滑膛槍，配刺刀，滑膛無後準星，用定裝紙包的火藥與布裹彈丸發射；民兵裝備混雜，有舊式滑膛槍、賓夕法尼亞式獵槍、散彈槍與短管手槍，彈藥靠各郡徵發的散裝火藥與鉛彈供應，數量常常不足；騎馬的志願兵隨身帶大口徑手槍，靠鞍袋裡的火藥與散裝彈丸裝填，射擊次數有限。索克與福克斯戰士的武器是獵槍與貿易得來的燧發滑膛槍，輔以弓、箭、戰斧與長柄矛，近身戰靠的是斧與矛而不是火器。火力的另一端在河上：汽船「戰士號」上架了一門可轉向的艦炮，居高臨下掃射渡河的隊伍，裝備差距就這樣被拉開。
kitsEn: The weapon on this card is the wheellock pistol, a product of Spanish and northern Italian locksmiths of the late fifteenth century: a tail holding priming powder at the rear, a mainspring barrel and ratchet in the middle, the spring driving a toothed wheel and axle, and a cock carrying a flint that struck the wheel face to raise the spark. The whole pistol cost far more than a contemporary musket, and cocking it was slow and required both hands, so it was issued only to officers and guards of the musket line, never to the rank and file in the line of battle. By 1832 the mechanism had been superseded by the flintlock for two full centuries and would not actually appear on any battlefield. The American regular infantry carried the Model 1816 flintlock smoothbore musket in .54 calibre, with bayonet; being smoothbore it had no rear sight, and it fired paper cartridges of powder and cloth-wrapped balls. Militia equipment was a mixture: old smoothbores, Pennsylvania rifles, shotguns and short-barrelled pistols, with ammunition drawn in bulk from county levies of loose powder and lead, and the supply was often short. Mounted volunteers carried large-calibre pistols at the saddle, loaded from the powder and loose balls in their saddlebags, and the number of rounds they could fire was limited. The weapons of the Sauk and Meskwaki warriors were hunting guns and trade flintlock smoothbores, backed by bows, arrows, tomahawks and long-handled spears; at close quarters the axe and the spear, not the firearm, did the work. The other end of the firepower lay on the river: the steamboat Warrior carried a swivel gun on her deck, and fired down on the people in the water, so that the gap in equipment opened wide.
tactics: 美方的戰術從一開始就受制於沒有騎兵。民兵多為獵戶出身，騎術生疏，志願騎兵在追擊途中常把馬留在後方、下馬作步槍射手使用，於是整支追擊縱隊實際上是一支步行縱隊，遠慢於熟悉河道與沼澤的索克隊伍。索克與福克斯的戰術是流動與拖延：戰士分成小隊沿河岸遊走，不願列陣會戰，每到一處就劫掠後撤，傷病與飢餓靠隨隊轉移的婦孺一同拖慢追兵。四月二十四日，黑鷹率約二百名戰士攻擊伊利諾伊州伊利莎白鎮附近的蘋果河堡，守軍只有二十至三十餘名民兵，堡內婦女裝彈壓藥，撐了約四十五分鐘，黑鷹才撤走。七月二十一日在威斯康辛河畔、如今的索克城一帶，黑鷹與尼亞波自任後衛，以約五十名索克人與六七十名基卡普人擋住七百五十名民兵，為非戰鬥員爭取渡河時間；民兵僅傷一人，卻造成對方多達六十八人的傷亡。八月初的巴茲艾克斯之戰，追擊縱隊沿河岸推進，志願騎兵與正規步兵交替下馬射擊，汽船「戰士號」沿密西根河橫掃，攔截正在渡河的人。開火之後，渡河的隊伍被壓回岸邊，河面成了雙方最無掩護的接觸面；黑鷹的隊伍在隨後數次追擊中被逐步消耗殆盡。
tacticsEn: American tactics were constrained from the outset by the absence of cavalry. Most of the militia were hunters with poor riding, and volunteer horsemen in pursuit commonly left their horses behind and fought on foot as riflemen, so that the whole pursuing column was in practice a walking column, far slower than a Sauk party that knew the rivers and the swamps. Sauk and Meskwaki tactics were movement and delay: the warriors moved in small bands along the river bank, declined pitched battle, looted and withdrew at every stop, and their wounded and hungry were slowed down by the women and children who moved with them. On 24 April Black Hawk attacked with some 200 warriors the Apple River Fort near Elizabeth, Illinois; the garrison was only twenty to thirty-odd militiamen, the women inside the fort moulded bullets and loaded muskets, and after about forty-five minutes Black Hawk broke off. On 21 July, on the Wisconsin River near what is now Sauk City, Black Hawk and Neapope took on the role of rear guard, holding about 50 Sauks and 60 to 70 Kickapoos against 750 militiamen to buy time for the non-combatants to cross the river; the militia lost one man, but inflicted as many as sixty-eight casualties on the other side. In the opening days of August the Battle of Bad Axe was fought with the column pushing along the bank, volunteer horse and regular foot alternating between mounted advance and dismounted shooting, while the steamboat Warrior swept the Mississippi and cut off those trying to cross. Once the firing started, the people in the water were driven back to the bank, and the river became the most exposed contact surface of the whole campaign; Black Hawk's column was then ground down piece by piece in the succeeding pursuits.
data: 戰役自一八三二年四月五日至八月二十七日，歷時五個多月。索克方在四月渡河時有五百名戰士與六百名老幼，總計約一千一百人；美方先後投入民兵六千餘人（僅伊利諾伊一州估計就有六千至七千人）、正規步兵六百三十人，另有聯盟原住民七百餘人。美方傷亡合計九十八人，其中陣亡六十人、受傷三十六人、被俘二人；另有平民、民兵與正規軍在戰役中死亡七十七人，不含斯科特部隊在霍亂中的亡故。索克方陣亡與被俘合計約二百九十七至三百三十三人，陣亡約二百二十二至二百五十八人、被俘七十五人。關鍵戰鬥的數字各異：五月十四日斯提爾曼河之夜戰，四十名戰士擊潰民兵營，擊斃十二人；七月二十一日威斯康辛高地之戰，七百五十名民兵對上約一百一十至一百二十名後衛戰士，美軍僅傷一人；八月二日巴茲艾克斯之戰，美軍陣亡十四人，其中一人是友軍誤傷的梅諾米尼人，仍以軍禮安葬。八月初，達科他與霍奇克武裝在密西根河東岸追擊殘部；九月，斯科特與雷諾茲先與霍奇克人立約，再與索克、福克斯立約，索克與福克斯割讓愛荷華東部約六百萬英畝土地，換取每年兩萬美元、為期三十年的補償款。
dataEn: The war ran from 5 April to 27 August 1832, a little over five months. The Sauk side entered the war with 500 warriors and 600 non-combatants, about 1,100 people in all; the Americans committed more than 6,000 militiamen (the Illinois contingent alone is estimated at six to seven thousand), 630 Army regulars, and over 700 allied Native fighters. American casualties came to 98 in all, of whom 60 were killed, 36 wounded and 2 captured; a further 77 settlers, militiamen and regulars died in the war, not counting the dead among Scott's relief force from cholera. Sauk losses were put at between 297 and 333 killed and captured, of whom 222 to 258 were killed and 75 captured. The figures for the individual actions differ sharply. At the night action on Stillman's Run on 14 May, forty warriors broke up the militia camp and killed twelve. At Wisconsin Heights on 21 July, 750 militiamen met about 110 to 120 rear-guard warriors and lost one man. At Bad Axe on 2 August the Americans lost fourteen men, one of them a Menominee killed by friendly fire who was still buried with military honours. In early August Dakota and Ho-Chunk parties hunted the remnants on the east bank of the Mississippi. In September Scott and Reynolds first concluded a treaty with the Ho-Chunks and then with the Sauks and Meskwakis, by which the latter ceded about six million acres in eastern Iowa for twenty thousand dollars a year for thirty years.
cause: 戰爭的起因是一紙被索克人視為詐騙的條約。一八〇四年《聖路易條約》把密西根河與羅克河之間的土地割予美國，卻容許兩族繼續耕種，直到政府把地賣給殖民者為止；一八二八年政府開始測量，印第安代理人托馬斯·福賽斯要索克人遷出索肯努克，黑鷹一派在一八三〇年春天帶著二百多名基卡普人重回老村，之後白人在冬季獵季住滿村莊，這支部眾名為「英國支隊」，並指望加拿大英軍的支援。一八三一年，西部軍區司令蓋恩斯調兵並要求伊利諾伊民兵提供騎兵營，六月末雙方在萬德魯夫島達成協議，黑鷹等首領簽字保證不再東渡。真正的爆點是美方的接觸政策：阿特金森四月十二日抵達羅克島，四月十三日寫信給州長雷諾茲，誇大了威脅，州長樂見其成，四月二十二日就在比爾茲敦召集民兵。四月十三日，瓦博基謝克派去的使者被美軍扣留；五月十二日少校哈克爾頓擅自獵殺一名索克人；五月十四日夜黑鷹夜襲斯提爾曼營，殺死十二名民兵。慘案傳開後，傑克遜與陸軍部長劉易斯·卡斯都拒絕外交解決，寧可要一場能震懾其他部族的徹底勝利。第一層是土地與主權，第二層是美方的行政失誤與誤報，第三層是總統與部長的政策，三者疊在一起，最終把一次遷徙爭端變成了兵戎相見。
causeEn: The war began with a treaty the Sauks regarded as a swindle. The Treaty of Saint Louis of 1804 ceded the land between the Mississippi and the Rock River to the United States, while allowing the two tribes to keep cultivating it until the government sold it to settlers; in 1828 the government began surveying the tract, and the Indian agent Thomas Forsyth told the Sauks to vacate Saukenuk. Black Hawk's faction returned to the old village in the spring of 1830 with more than two hundred Kickapoos, and when white families occupied the village during the winter hunting season, the band was known as the British Band and looked to the British at Fort Malden in Canada for support. In 1831 General Edmund Gaines, commander of the Western Department, mustered troops and asked the Illinois militia for a mounted battalion, and at the end of June the two sides reached an agreement on Vandruff Island in which Black Hawk and other leaders signed a promise to stay west of the Mississippi. The real fuse was American contact policy. Atkinson reached Rock Island on 12 April, wrote to Governor Reynolds on 13 April and exaggerated the threat, and Reynolds, eager for a war, called out the militia at Beardstown on 22 April. On 13 April emissaries sent by Wabokieshiek were detained by the Americans; on 12 May Major Hackelton killed a Sauk on his own initiative; and on the night of 14 May Black Hawk attacked Stillman's camp and killed twelve militiamen. Once the news of the massacre spread, both Jackson and Secretary of War Lewis Cass refused any diplomatic solution, wanting a resounding victory that would serve as an example to other tribes. The first layer was land and sovereignty, the second American administrative error and bad intelligence, the third the policy of the President and the Secretary; layered together they turned a migration dispute into a shooting war.
impact: 這場戰爭的後果，超出了戰場本身。索克與福克斯失去愛荷華東部的土地，部眾被推向密西根河西岸與更遠的堪薩斯保留地；霍奇克人也在同年秋天的約定中割出威斯康辛河以南的土地，換取愛荷華一條四十英里寬的地帶與每年一萬美元、為期二十七年的補償，那塊地帶被稱為「中立地帶」。戰爭證明了美國陸軍的短板：全軍沒有騎兵，追擊敵人只能靠臨時招募的志願騎兵，戰後國會在道奇率領下成立騎兵營，一八三三年擴編成第一騎兵團，此後山地與西部騎兵成為美軍常設建制。政治上，這是一場美國的選舉造星戰：至少七名後來的美國參議員、四名伊利諾伊州州長，以及密歇根、內布拉斯加與威斯康辛屬地未來的州長都參與其中，日後的兩位總統泰勒與林肯也在此役中初露頭角。林肯沒打一仗，卻在民兵營裡鍛煉出處理危機與維持軍紀的本事。另一面，這場戰爭被援引為美國印地安人遷移政策的辯護：既然索克人「自己選擇戰爭」，土地便可以被沒收，遷移便可以被說成是他們的命運。戰後數月的強制西遷途中又遇霍亂流行，隊伍在途中崩潰，而這段慘事在官方敘述裡很少被提及。
impactEn: The consequences of the Black Hawk War reached far beyond the battlefield. The Sauks and Meskwakis lost their lands in eastern Iowa and their people were pushed towards the west bank of the Mississippi and on to the Kansas reservation; the Ho-Chunks, in the settlement concluded that autumn, ceded everything south of the Wisconsin River in exchange for a strip forty miles wide in Iowa and ten thousand dollars a year for twenty-seven years, a tract known as the Neutral Ground. The war also exposed a weakness in the United States Army: it had no cavalry at all, and pursuit of the enemy depended on hastily raised volunteer horsemen; after the campaign Congress created a mounted battalion under Henry Dodge, expanded into the 1st Cavalry Regiment in 1833, and from then on mountain and western horse were permanent establishments of the army. In political terms the war was a maker of American careers: at least seven future United States senators, four future governors of Illinois and future governors of Michigan, Nebraska and the Wisconsin Territory all took part, and the two future presidents Taylor and Lincoln first showed themselves here. Lincoln fought no battle, but in the militia camp he trained the habits that later served him in handling a crisis and keeping discipline. On the other side, the war was used to argue for American Indian removal: if the Sauks had chosen war, then their land could be taken and their removal could be presented as their fate. The forced marches west that followed broke down in the cholera that summer, and that part of the story was rarely told in the official accounts.
result: 美方全勝，而且是一場由民兵主導、正規軍殿後的勝利。四月到五月，聯軍沿羅克河搜索，至五月二十八日惠特塞德旅在奧塔瓦解散，只留下約三百人再留二十日；阿特金森重組的「邊疆軍」自六月起才真正成形，七月十五日道奇與詹姆斯·D·亨利自溫尼巴戈堡出發追擊，七月二十一日在威斯康辛高地擊潰黑鷹的後隊，迫使非戰鬥員渡河，八月二日聯軍在巴茲艾克斯河畔與密西根河上展開最後一擊，擊潰剩餘部眾。黑鷹本人與瓦博基謝克於八月二十七日在普雷里杜欣向印第安代理人約瑟夫·斯特里特投降，柴契利·泰勒接管囚犯，傑斐遜·戴維斯與羅伯特·安德森以汽船押送他們順流而下往傑斐遜兵營；黑鷹等二十名首領被囚，翌年四月轉送維吉尼亞的門羅堡，四月二十六日在華盛頓受到傑克遜接見，並在囚禁期間為畫家畫像、公開場合露面。留在密西根河西岸的索克與福克斯，首領基奧庫克與瓦佩洛代表兩族，於一八三二年九月與斯科特、雷諾茲達成割地協議；索克人雖然同時失去了首領、土地與家園，但部族的生存得以延續，基奧庫克獲得了保留地與「首席首領」的名分。戰役的軍事結果清楚：索克人作為密西根河以東的有效軍事力量就此終結，黑鷹最後的追擊被掃平，美國在密西根河東岸的軍事控制再無對手。
resultEn: The Americans won outright, and it was a victory carried by the militia with the regulars bringing up the rear. From April to May the combined force searched up the Rock River, and on 28 May Whiteside's brigade disbanded at Ottawa, Illinois, with only about 300 men staying on for another twenty days. The Army of the Frontier reconstituted by Atkinson only really took shape from June; on 15 July Dodge and James D. Henry marched out of Fort Winnebago in pursuit, on 21 July they broke Black Hawk's rear guard at Wisconsin Heights and forced the non-combatants across the river, and on 2 August the combined force struck the remnants on the banks of the Bad Axe and on the Mississippi and destroyed them. Black Hawk himself and Wabokieshiek surrendered at Prairie du Chien on 27 August to the Indian agent Joseph Street; Zachary Taylor took custody of the prisoners, and Jefferson Davis and Robert Anderson carried them down the Mississippi by steamboat to Jefferson Barracks. Black Hawk and nineteen other leaders were imprisoned, and in the following April he and four others were transferred to Fort Monroe in Virginia; on 26 April they were received by President Jackson in Washington and posed for the artists who painted them in captivity. Those Sauks and Meskwakis who remained west of the Mississippi, represented by Keokuk and Wapello, concluded the cession treaty with Scott and Reynolds in September 1832. The tribe had lost its leaders, its lands and its home at one stroke, but it survived as a people, and Keokuk obtained both a reservation and the standing of principal chief. The military result is plain: as an effective military force east of the Mississippi the Sauks ceased to exist, the last of Black Hawk's pursuers was swept away, and American military control of the east bank of the Mississippi met no further opposition.
